# 17 — Decision ledger (the owner's one-pass veto review)

Campaigner is built autonomously: across the pipeline the dispatcher made
default calls on the owner's behalf — everything reversible, everything
recorded here, everything reviewable in one pass. Every decision below is
**Status: active** in the shipped code — re-verified landing by landing against
`main` (the last full pass was the consolidation that landed this line, at
`main` @ `79abe82`: 236 files / 2727 tests passing under the bounded gate
`pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`, lint 0 problems, typecheck clean). That
baseline is a DATE STAMP, not a claim about HEAD — it is not re-frozen on every
docs commit, so a stale-looking number means "re-run the gate", not "the ledger
is wrong"; nothing here is verified by a remembered count. The enumeration is
complete: no standing default lives outside this
list. The binding spec text stays in the referenced doc/section — where a
row and its reference disagree, the reference wins.

Coverage/pruning/initiative/rail stay kind-agnostic and byte-unchanged (today’s kind-blind coverage is already fog-shaped). WHY THE EARLIER DECISION WAS OVERTURNED: its reasoning (“not to blind the GM”) did not describe the actual risk — tokens still paint ABOVE the veils by DOM order, and the GM can drag a fog aside, delete it, or lift it with “Reveal next room” — while at ~10% the two kinds rendered identically, which was the reported bug. The veil rail's labels are kind-aware (it resolves the selected RECORD, not just its id): "Delete fog"/"Resize fog n" for a fog, veil for a veil; test ids stay family ids. NO MIGRATION: `kind` is persisted board data, so an already-seeded battle keeps its fog covers (still blocking, now cloud-filled) until re-seeded from its encounter. It is deliberately NOT a "is the prose specific?" judgement — a threshold is exactly what an LLM answers inconsistently and then rationalises after the fact — so there is no threshold anywhere in the mechanism. One writer path, one provenance story, one failure story; the chat's whole intellectual load becomes one call. **The seam** is `src/features/modules/change-artifact.ts` — `changeArtifact({ artifactId, instruction?, encounter? })`. It resolves the row, chooses the route from `artifact.kind` (never from a claim the caller makes) and forwards. The seam therefore invents no run input — the instruction rides the BRIEF the specialist already builds, in ONE implementation (`llm/additionalInstruction`, which `runEngine`'s four sites render through as well). Two consequences are stated because they are load-bearing: the brief persists as the run row's `userBrief`, so a resumed run keeps the instruction; and the brief is also the retrieval query and the grounding-detection text, so an instruction participates in grounding — accepted (it is the same free-text field, and grounding on the requested change is the better error). Per kind: `buildEntityBrief` gained a trailing optional `instruction` (its final paragraph, carried by the entity lane's `RunEntityBatchInput.instruction`), and `EncounterRegenOptions.instruction` reaches EVERY brief the operation sends — the content leg, the single path's map leg and the prose leg; the prose leg keeps its own prose-only + roster-verbatim contract, so a reply that lets the instruction override it fails loud with nothing half-applied. **Empty means absent, byte-for-byte:** `additionalInstructionSection('')` is `null` and `withAdditionalInstruction(brief, '')` returns the brief UNCHANGED — no separator, no empty paragraph. That is why the artifact editor's two long-standing buttons (which pass no instruction) keep sending exactly the prompts they always sent, and why every existing full-literal brief/contract pin still guards the default. **The refusals — returned as values, never reported as success.** A bestiary creature row is REFUSED with the shared `creature-row-guard.creatureRowAiRefusal` copy, nothing written and no engine called. A module-less entity row is refused (the entity engines ground every brief in the owning module's text, so there is nothing to ground in — the reason names the way out). `pc` and `plotarc` are UNSUPPORTED: the Party is authored (row 69) and a plot arc is a real artifact kind with a real engine but is not a module entity kind (`ENTITY_KINDS` has no plotarc; this arc extends no vocabulary). A kind-option mismatch (encounter options on an npc, no operation for an encounter) THROWS: that is a programming error, not a user-facing refusal. **THE CREATURE-ROW REFUSAL IS A RATIFIED BOUNDARY** (owner's standing decision for this arc, verbatim: **"the bestiary creature-row refusal STANDS. It is the ONE documented exception to 'change any artifact from an instruction'."**): a rulebook-cited, chunk-backed creature row is ONE shared row per campaign per cited chunk, pointed at by every citing encounter, with battle seeding resolving its stats through it and its portrait cached globally — it is an identity, not an authoring slot, and it is never rewritable by instruction. The refusal carries its named reason and the remedy, writes nothing at all, and can never be reported as success, so a caller (later, the chat) can see WHY and relay it to the owner instead of appearing to fail silently. This is a deliberate exception, not debt and not a TODO: do not "fix" it later. **Uniform semantics, not new ones.** The one-generation-per-module gate is the EXISTING `llm/canvasBusy` registry — claimed for the change, released in `finally`, second claimant gets the existing loud `ModuleBusyError` (never a queue, never a silent no-op). Failures PROPAGATE (AGENTS 1/2): a specialist that throws, a run that did not complete carrying the specialist's own reason, a vanished campaign or module. The only non-throwing outcomes are the seam's own decisions, returned as a discriminated result — `changed` (with the `operation` that ran), `refused` (with its `reason`) and `unsupported` (with its `reason`), every arm carrying `artifactId` and `kind` — so a caller branches without matching a string. Provenance and persistence stay the specialist's write. **NO UNDO STORY IS INVENTED — the honest position.** Artifact ROWS have no versions and no undo: the module DOCUMENT has durable versions (`moduleVersionRepo`), an artifact row has only its own revisions (which `updateArtifact` writes before a content write) plus the documented regeneration semantics — a regenerated artifact legitimately loses what regeneration replaces. | 100 | **Every wiki-link chip's hover tooltip LEADS with the byte-exact token it was written from — because the plugin that builds the chip had thrown the source bytes away** (owner request, verbatim: *"i would like to have a hover tooltip over all Wikilinks where the raw text of the link is displayed. `hast-util-to-jsx-runtime` hands it to the React component) — and `WikiMdNode` grew a deliberate minimal `data` view rather than a cast. **VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY rather than assumed**, because a documented carrier that silently does not survive would leave the tooltip empty while every pin passed on the fallback: a scratch probe against react-markdown 10.1.0 / mdast-util-to-hast 13.2.1 rendered `<a href="#wiki:Ash%20Gate" data-wiki-raw="[[ Encounter:Ash Gate \|the gate]]">the gate</a>` and the `a` component received `href, data-wiki-raw, node, children` — so `hProperties` IS the mechanism and no fallback was needed. (2) The chip's tooltip is `wikiChipTitle(raw, existing) = \`${raw} — ${existing}\`` — the token FIRST, and **every existing title survives byte-intact as the tail**: resolved `[[ Ash Gate \|the gate]] — NPC Ash Gate`, unresolved `[[Kael]] — Kael — not detailed yet`, ambiguous `[[Ash Gate]] — ⚠ 2 artifacts match “Ash Gate”: …`. The token is also set on the chip element as `data-wiki-raw`, so the carrier is inspectable independently of the tooltip string. (3) **The mechanism is the native `title`, chosen deliberately**: the chip is a real, non-`disabled` `<button>`, so its tooltip renders (docs/18 §4's invisible-`title` defect is measured for natively disabled controls only — a disabled shadcn Button is not even hit-tested), and it adds NO wrapper element inside flowing prose — chips are `inline-flex` in module prose and a reader renders many of them, so a tooltip trigger per chip risks layout drift at reader scale; `BlockedControl` is NOT used (nothing here is blocked). **Surface coverage is automatic, and the audit is the reason to believe it**: `#wiki:` hrefs have exactly ONE producer (`wikiHref`) and exactly ONE consumer (`wiki-markdown`), and every wiki-aware surface renders through that one `WikiMarkdown` — module reader, canvas preview, peek modal, artifact-body preview (`markdown-body`), part-text-editor preview, all three module-board card kinds, and the guide. FIELD-level GM material is still keyed on the DOCUMENT audience (faction `methods`, encounter `tactics`/`treasure`/`terrain`, PC `notes`, the part plan, the treasure ledger), because that is the leak boundary: a section declared `all` prints for players WITHOUT its GM fields. (2) What a hidden\|frozen page DOES break is the 1 Hz WALL-CLOCK watchdog in `llm/openrouter.readStream`: it compared `Date.now()` deltas, so the suspended gap counted as silence and it called `reader.cancel()` on a healthy stream — and after a resume the post-loop diagnosis (:637-659) re-derived the same failure from the same clocks EVEN AFTER A CLEAN `done` close (`if (done) break` at :607 falls straight through into it), so a provider that ends the body instead of sending `[DONE]` had its COMPLETE answer thrown away as `content-stall`\|`max-duration`. (3) The WORST case was a discarded\|reloaded tab: `runRepo.failRunningRuns` reconciles RUN rows at boot, but NOTHING reconciled a MODULE row, so a module mid-generation stayed `'generating'` FOREVER — a permanent spinner, a Stop button that was a silent no-op (`cancelModuleGen` on a module with no live controller is `controllers.get(id)?.abort()`), every retry affordance gated behind `!busy`, and "Stop all generations" counting that dead row as stopped and toasting that it had stopped it. **The status is a LEASE, and the fix names the guard.** `llm/moduleGenReconcile` is the ONE place that decides whether a `'generating'` row is owned: `moduleGen.hasLiveModuleGen(id)` (THIS page's controller registry) OR a held Web Lock named `campaigner:generation:module-gen:<id>` (the cross-tab lease, `lib/generationLocks`). App START reconciles every row that says `'generating'` and nobody owns: the row lands `'failed'` with a NAMED sentence (`INTERRUPTED_MODULE_GEN_MESSAGE`: the page writing it is gone, finished parts are untouched, unfinished ones are back to pending, press "Resume module generation"), every part slot still at `'generating'` rewinds to `'pending'`, and the batch entry point toasts the count. Nothing is reset silently, nothing already written is touched, and the guard is RE-EVALUATED INSIDE the write transaction (`moduleRepo.failInterruptedModuleGen` takes the predicate), so a pass that registers between the read and the write cannot be failed. Because the rewind lands the module in exactly the state `generateMissingParts` already recovers from, the recovery path needed no new machinery (pinned end to end: the rewound part is written by `generateMissingParts` and the finished part is not re-run) and the reader's own `!busy` gate opens with its failed banner + **Resume module generation** + **Generate missing parts** enabled. **Start is the load-bearing moment, and that was a second defect.** The three boot calls (`failRunningRuns`, `seedBuiltInPersonas`, `ensurePersistentStorage`) sat in `AppShell`'s RENDER BODY, so EVERY re-render — a theme toggle, the help dialog, any store change — re-ran them, and `failRunningRuns` fails every `'running'` row: an unrelated UI change could fail a live run. They are a mount effect now, and the module reconciliation runs there too (a discarded tab RELOADS, so it gets no `visibilitychange` at all). The visibility path is the second chance, not the main one: on `visibilitychange`\|`freeze`\|`resume`\|`pagehide`\|`pageshow` the page records the SUSPENDED GAP (`lib/pageLiveness`) and reconciles module rows again — deliberately NOT runs, because a hidden tab keeps running its engine and failing those rows would invent the very defect this row removes. **Every Stop control tells the truth, and "Stop all" counts only work it did.** `moduleGenReconcile.stopModuleGeneration` is the ONE behaviour behind the reader's Stop and the board's Stop: a live controller in this page → `cancelModuleGen` (a real abort, unchanged); another tab holds the generation lock → nothing is stopped and nothing is failed, and it SAYS SO ("Another tab is generating this module — press Stop there."); nobody owns the row → it is reconciled (real work: the loud failed state + rewind); the row already settled → it says that too. Silence is the bug in all four cases. `features/progress/stop-all-generations` keeps its exact count of DISTINCT stopped units but now asks the same guard: a live forge is cancelled and counted, an unclaimed row is reconciled and counted SEPARATELY (`{ stopped, reconciled }`, the reconciled rows toasted as the loud interrupted report), and when nothing was stopped but a dead row was reconciled it no longer claims "Nothing was running" (pinned: the row is failed with its recovery sentence and `cancelModuleGen` is never called). **The watchdog now measures liveness, and reports only a limit it ARMED.** `readStream` computes its three deltas through `lib/pageLiveness.activeElapsedMs` (wall time MINUS the gaps the page reported), and the post-loop diagnosis fires only for the limit the watchdog actually tripped (`trippedLimit`), so a clean close after a long silence returns the accumulated text. Both directions are pinned, because the cheap wrong fix here is a looser limit: a gap far beyond the content-stall limit does NOT kill a healthy stream (which then completes normally), a clean close after a ten-minute suspension returns the COMPLETE answer, and a stream that really died STILL fails — after the resume, on the same 2s\|3s limits, as `stalled after 2s of silence` — plus the keep-alive-only case that must still trip `content-stall`. Nothing about the limits themselves moved. **Two cheap, documented freeze mitigations.** (1) Every generation PASS (spine, parts, post-generation sweep) runs inside `withGenerationLock(moduleGenLockName(id), …)`: Chromium's published freeze criteria list "the page holds a Web Lock" as an opt-out, and the same lock is the cross-tab lease above. It is ADVISORY, NEVER A DEPENDENCY: with no Web Locks API the work runs directly, an unavailable lock still runs the work (a second tab generating the same module was already possible and must not become a new failure mode), and nothing branches on whether it was granted. (2) `lib/backgroundTitle` writes `document.title` while the tab is HIDDEN only — `Working: <label> — Campaigner`, `✓ Finished: …`, `⚠ Failed: …` (failed outranks finished outranks running, extras counted as `(+N more)`) — because the tab strip is the only surface a backgrounded page has, and a page that keeps producing observable output is not the page the freeze heuristics pick. A USER STOP reaches no verdict: the entry is cleared, so the title can never invent "finished". **The wait for a run rides the ROW, not a timer.** `waitForRunStatus` slept in chained 250 ms `setTimeout` calls; Chromium throttles a hidden page's timers to about one wake-up a MINUTE, and a chain or batch step boundary is exactly where this is awaited — the shape of the owner's report. It now awaits `runRepo.waitForRunRowChange` (a Dexie `liveQuery` over the run row, resolving on any change or on the row disappearing), with the abort semantics and the "row disappeared" contract preserved to the character, and it is pinned structurally: NO 250 ms timer is scheduled while the wait is pending. **A completed run keeps no stale interruption message.** The step-outcome write now clears `errorMessage`\|`failureKind` along with restoring `'running'`, so a run the old render-body `failRunningRuns()` had wrongly marked failed is LIVE and truthful again at its next step — and the completion write, the in-loop cancel and `cancel(runId)` clear it too. The residue was a `'completed'` row still reading "Interrupted by reload". MEASURED, and reported rather than rounded up: the step write's clearing is injection-proven (removing it fails the pin), while the completion write's is REDUNDANT today — removing it leaves the suite green, because every path to completion passes a step write — and is kept, with a comment saying so, so a future path that completes without a step write cannot resurrect the defect. **NOT built, deliberately (the brief's own exclusions, upheld).** No partial-stream journaling and no Web Worker orchestration: the owner's ask is that the browser keep giving the app resources, and a journal would be a new storage seam with its own reconciliation problem, while a Worker would move the same timers into another thread that is throttled and frozen identically. The module PDF\|export\|plan seam and the creature\|cast arcs are untouched. **Honest limits.** (1) NO test in this repo can FREEZE a page or throttle its timers — jsdom has no freeze, no discard and no timer throttling — so the freeze MITIGATION is documented (Chromium's published opt-out criteria) and the gap crediting is pinned by driving the very events the browser fires (`visibilitychange`\|`freeze`\|`resume`), NOT by observing a real freeze: that half of the owner's original question stays UNPROVEN in tests by construction, and docs/08-TESTING.md says so in the same words. (2) The watchdog timer itself is unchanged (1 Hz), so on a frozen page it wakes up late — now harmless, because the gap is credited and the stream survives — which means a dead stream is still detected, just later than it would be on a visible page. (3) The cross-tab lease is Web Locks, so in a browser WITHOUT that API a second tab cannot see another tab's forge: start-time reconciliation there can fail a row a live other tab is writing. It is self-healing (that pass rewrites the status on its next part boundary and completes normally), but a transient spurious failure is possible and is stated here rather than hidden. (4) The tiny race where a resumed pass registers its controller just after the reconcile's read is self-healing for the same reason. Refusals are named, never guessed (no clamping, no rounding, never the chip's display label): a point strictly inside a wiki chip says a chip is replaced as its whole token, a cross-part selection says one span inside one part, an unmapped span (inline code, an image, the unwritten-part placeholder) says so, an empty selection says select first, and a capture measured against an OLDER document says select again. **Where the capture lives, and why.** `previewStore.selectionByModule` (per module, session-only like the toggle): a click on the header button COLLAPSES the browser selection, so it cannot be read at confirm time, and the dialog must show the same text it captured — so `CanvasPreview` captures on `selectionchange` plus the pane's mouse/key release (collapsed selections report nothing, so the click that consumes the capture cannot erase it), and `CanvasPage` re-resolves it against the LIVE document when the dialog opens AND when the action runs. The alternative (a fingerprint of the planned-from structure) would need a NEW field on the plan, and this slice must not widen `documentPlanSchema` (rule 5 of the brief; the schema, the role vocabulary and the renderer layout are untouched). **WHAT STORAGE IS STILL FOR, now that it is not a cache.** Two things, both real: (a) the row is the RECORD of what the last export decided — the only evidence available when a book comes out badly, and what the "Document plan" surface inspects; (b) it is the ESCAPE HATCH — when the planning call FAILS, the export renders whatever plan the row still holds (the LAST book, byte-identical structure, no call spent) instead of nothing. **WHAT THIS TRADES AWAY, stated as a decision and not as an accident:** the same module exported twice now yields TWO DIFFERENT BOOKS whenever the model decides differently, because row 109's reproducibility guarantee ("a stored plan renders the same document twice") is now scoped to a stored `(module, plan)` — the RENDERER is still deterministic and byte-for-byte (row 109's measured 6359-character definition and 51271-byte PDF are untouched, re-pinned green), but two consecutive EXPORTS no longer share a plan. The owner accepted this knowingly, on the grounds that two exports of an unchanged module are rare; the escape hatch above is what keeps the case he DID describe ("re-exporting because the previous book was wrong" — or because the provider was down) from costing him either a call or the last book. **FAILURE IS LOUD IN TWO PLACES, AND THE EXPORT STILL LANDS** (AGENTS rules 1–2): a planning failure (busy module, transport, invalid reply, a plan naming something that does not exist) raises `toastError('Could not plan the document — exporting without a fresh plan', error)` — the raw cause, named — while the document is built anyway from the row as it stands, and the document CARRIES the verdict itself through the new `ModulePdfInput.planFailure`: an alert page that says either *"This document was laid out from the module's LAST STORED document plan: the automatic planning step for this export failed — <reason>"* or, with no stored plan, *"…from the procedural outline: the automatic planning step for this export failed — <reason>"*, plus a `the document plan` entry in the export's `problems` list (so the export's own toast repeats it). Rationale for landing rather than aborting: the renderer's contract is that missing data is a visible defect INSIDE the document, never a lost document, and a PDF export needs no provider — aborting would have taken away the ability to print ANY module document while the LLM is unreachable, which is a capability the owner had before this row. The two documents are never confusable: the reason is on the page, and the toast is an error, not a success. | 148 | **THE MODULE PDF IS PAGED, NOT FLOWED: a main column with the mechanics in a sidebar beside it, and only the oversized things get a page of their own** (owner, verbatim: *"PDF is still completely one dimensional flowing, no sidebars and nothing interesting happening at all."*). There is nothing to disambiguate, so the book is not even READ on this arm (the lazy `titleFor`/`describe` readers keep the common case free, exactly as their own comment claimed), and using the library's one candidate is not a guess: it is the only answer the library has. Both non-narrowing shapes throw THE SAME sentence: it is one ambiguity with one remedy, and the candidate list already carries every real title, so a separate "the book you named matched nothing" clause would be a second message saying what the list says. The count in that sentence is now `sameName.length` rather than the narrowed set's — strictly more honest in the one case they differ: a named book holding two of three same-named creatures used to print *"holds 2 creatures of that name (Zombie (Bestiary), Zombie (Bestiary))"*, naming one book twice while hiding the third candidate; it now names all three with their books. Expensive per-row resolution STOPS as soon as the running cost passes the cap, so the DB reads a row that cannot be sent would need are never spent. **WHAT IS UNTOUCHED (the pins the brief bound):** `modulePlannerReplySchema` / `MODULE_PLAN_CONTRACT_NAME`, `documentPlanIssues` (every `source` names ONE thing in the inventory; an id/index not in it fails the WHOLE plan), `planAndStoreModuleDocument` (the ONE plan write) and the renderer (`lib/modulePdf`) are all unchanged. **PINS** (`tests/llm/modulePlan.test.ts`, 14 → 20): the content pin asserts the built message carries the module's OWN text and a row's FULL stored prose including the part past 160 chars (`THE-FAR-END-OF-THE-ROW`); the link-map pin asserts `premise: «Old Tower» (location <id>)` from the real graph; the empty-row pin asserts the named `NOT RENDERED` line; the cap pin (an over-budget pool) asserts `[BLOCK FULL`, the cap number, and that the marker NAMES both the overflowing row and the one after it; two assembler pins assert `[TRUNCATED` names its block and that a fitting block carries NO marker. | 173 | **THE IDEA BOARD LANDS — a standalone plain-text writing surface at `/idea-board`, ONE app-level row, and the module chat is deliberately NOT reused** (owner request, verbatim: *"I want to introduce a new functionality into the app that is not really connected with any other system, but can be used for basically everything. Its just an edit box with a left sidebar (similar to module chat) where the user can paste a text, then refine it with the LLM. With a small copy button so the text is then easily copied into whatever the user wants. Similar to the chatgpt canvas. I guess a lot of the module chat functionality can be reused for this."*). **THE INTENT, extracted before scoping:** the felt problem is a SCRATCH SURFACE — paste anything, talk it through with a model, copy the result out — and "similar to module chat" describes the SHAPE the owner wants (edit box + left sidebar + a small copy affordance), not a mandate to wire the module protocol into it. The literal "a lot of the module chat functionality can be reused" is the one part of the ask that had to be answered with evidence rather than followed: MEASURED at HEAD, `llm/canvasChat.sendCanvasChatMessage`, `features/modules/canvas/chatTurn.runCanvasChatTurn` and `chatStore` are module-shaped end to end — they split a parts document (`splitModulePartsDocument`), ground every request on the campaign premise and ALL preceding modules' full text, resolve wiki-links against the artifact pool, claim a one-generation-per-`moduleId` registry, persist into `modules.chatThread` and reply with `<edit>`/`<request>`/`<change>` commands that MUTATE ARTIFACTS through `changeArtifact`. A board has no module id, no parts, no campaign and no entities, so reusing that protocol would import the very semantics the owner excluded ("normal text without any wikilinks"). What IS reused is everything BELOW the contract, and each is an existing seam: `openrouter.chat` (API key, escalation, strict structured outputs, language directive, retries, stream watchdogs, abort), `jsonReply.parseJsonReply` + zod, `strictSchema.schemaResponseFormat`, `generatedTextHygiene.generatedTextScanForFields`, `db/settingsRepo`, `lib/progress`, `lib/pageFlush`, `features/progress/stop-all-generations`, `lib/clipboard`, and the CodeMirror theme. **WHAT LANDED.** (1) **Route/IA** — `ROUTES.ideaBoard` = `/idea-board`, an APP-LEVEL route in the primary nav before Rules (`appNavItems`); `campaignIdFromPath` returns `undefined` there, so the campaign bar shows its disabled-tabs state and the New Module button hides — the board opens with NO campaign, which is what "usable for basically everything" requires. (2) **Storage** — ONE row in the additive Dexie **v23** table `ideaBoards` (`'id, updatedAt'`, no upgrade body; an older database starts with none and `ideaBoardRepo.getIdeaBoard` creates it inside ONE rw transaction so two concurrent opens cannot mint two boards). `saveIdeaBoard(next, expected)` is an in-transaction COMPARE-AND-SWAP against the snapshot the session loaded, so a second tab's write is refused loudly instead of silently overwritten. `domain/ideaBoard.parseIdeaBoards` REFUSES 2+ stored rows by name (one board is the contract; a restore that would pick or silently discard one is not acceptable), and the same function runs inside `importBackup` BEFORE its destructive write. The board rides the FULL-APP BACKUP (`ideaBoards` in `backup.OPTIONAL_TABLES`, so a pre-v23 zip restores EMPTY — the truth about that database) and deliberately does NOT ride a campaign export. (3) **Plain text, provably** — the editor is CodeMirror with `plainEditorTheme` and NO markdown language and NO wiki decorations; `tests/features/idea-board.test.tsx` types `Original [[literal]]` and asserts the accepted document contains those literal characters. (4) **The sidebar** — conversation + session model selection (blank = `settings.defaultChatModel`) + instruction box (Return sends, Shift+Return newlines), a `md:w-80` left column: the module chat's shape without its protocol. (5) **The copy button** — a header control that copies the whole document through the new ONE clipboard seam. (6) **Previous drafts** — accepting a suggestion (or restoring a draft) snapshots the text it replaces, giving the board its own undo for MODEL writes (CodeMirror history owns typing). **THE REFINEMENT CONTRACT** (`llm/ideaBoard.refineIdeaBoard`): ONE `chat` call whose system prompt states the surface's rules (ordinary text, NO wiki-links/app markup; answer in `reply`; the COMPLETE resulting text in `document` when asked to write/rewrite/restructure, `null` for a question or discussion), the stored transcript as history, and a final `{ document, instruction }` JSON turn; the reply is `parseJsonReply` + `ideaBoardReplySchema.parse`, and `modelUsed` comes from the call that actually served it (the escalation winner, never a settings lookup). It is grounded on the document AS OF SEND TIME. Every failure is loud and NAMED: an empty instruction throws before any call; a non-JSON reply fails the parse; a whitespace-only replacement is refused by name (the strict decoder strips `minLength`, so the PARSED value is checked); and the shared hygiene scan refuses escape debris or our own scaffolding echoed back before the text can be accepted. **THE TWO RULES THAT PROTECT THE OWNER'S TEXT, each pinned.** (a) **A refinement NEVER writes the document**: the reply lands as a `proposal` and `replaceIdeaDocument` — the only model-write path — snapshots the CURRENT draft into `versions` first, so accepting onto text that MOVED while the model thought still leaves the replaced text recoverable (the test types during the request, then accepts, then restores). (b) **The owner's instruction is recorded BEFORE the call**, so a FAILED or STOPPED turn never discards what they typed (module-chat parity); the stop test asserts the instruction survives while nothing is applied and nothing is proposed. A failed SAVE keeps the draft in memory with a humanized reason and a `Retry saving` control, with NO automatic retry loop — the compare-and-swap's "another tab changed this" refusal would otherwise be reported forever. **THE SALVAGE, recorded because it is part of the history:** the first writer DIED before finishing and left the whole slice UNCOMMITTED in the shared tree (no branch, no commit) — the audit found the code coherent and worth keeping, then verified it as a fresh landing rather than trusting it, which is what caught three real defects: (i) `IdeaBoardPatch` was declared `Pick<…>` instead of `Partial<Pick<…>>`, so typecheck failed on every `editIdeaBoard` call — a genuine break, unnoticed because the writer never ran the toolchain; (ii) the writer recorded the user turn only AFTER a successful reply, so a failed or stopped refinement DISCARDED the owner's typed instruction; (iii) the reply schema and the module-side hygiene scan had never been exercised, so the LLM contract had no test at all. All three are fixed here and each new behaviour is pinned. **THE DELETE-ALL-DATA ANSWER, stated rather than assumed:** `maintenance.deleteAllData` deletes the entire IndexedDB database, so the board IS taken by Settings → Delete all data (it is data, not a preference like the theme in `PRESERVED_KEYS`), while NO campaign or module wipe (`deleteCampaign`, `removeAllGeneratedContent`, `deleteCampaignWorkspace`) can reach it — it is not campaign-keyed. **COPIES: 2→1 — `src/lib/clipboard.copyText` carries the ONE `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, with both hand-rolled `persona-panel.tsx` call sites folded onto it (one of which lacked the availability check entirely); held by `tests/architecture/clipboard-seam.test.ts`, which reds on a third spelling. The editor theme is 2→1 (`lib/editorTheme.editorThemeSpec`, with `canvasTheme` composing it and `canvasThemeSpec` re-exported so the existing spec pins and markdown highlighting are unchanged). The board's own seams are each single-site: COPIES: 1 — checked, no duplication (grepped: runCanvasChatTurn, applyChatCommands, writeText, EditorView.theme, chat(, getSettings) — no second turn controller, applier, theme or transport was created.** **NUMBERS.** The landing gate (`bash scripts/gate.sh`, raw log `/tmp/gate-idea-board-2.log`, chunk logs `/tmp/gate-4100696`) printed **GATE GREEN, exit 0: 338 files / 3975 tests**, `chunk arithmetic: 338 of 338 test files covered`, lint 0 errors, typecheck clean, no `Errors:` line, peak RSS **1236 MB of the 3000 MB cap**; chunks `tests_lib 32/369 (834MB)`, `tests_llm 71/1158 (874MB)`, `tests_db 33/370 (657MB)`, `tests_domain 22/309 (693MB)`, `tests_features 136/1334 (1236MB)`, `tests_remainder 44/435 (1146MB)`. | 174 | **THE IDEA BOARD'S WHITE SQUARE AND WASTED HEIGHT ARE TWO LAYOUT BUGS, NOT A THEME — and the theme fix I reached for first is kept only as parity, which the package source disproved as the cause** (owner report, verbatim: *"The board looks like a big white square. white on white maybe? And the vertical space is not really used."*). **THE DIAGNOSIS, corrected against evidence rather than asserted.** The obvious suspect was the missing `theme="none"` — `canvasEditor.tsx` documents an owner-reported "white slab" on the unthemed mount and passes it, and the board (row 173) did not. Inspected in the INSTALLED package before acting, that suspect does not hold: `@uiw/react-codemirror`'s `theme` prop is used ONLY to choose a class name (`cm-theme-light` / `cm-theme-none` — the default is `'light'`) and contributes NO extension, no shipped CSS in the package or in this repo defines either class, and `@codemirror/view`'s base theme sets no background at all (its `&light` chrome is gutters, panels and a pale active-line tint). An unthemed editor is transparent, so it shows its wrapper's `bg-card` — DARK in dark mode. The white square was therefore (1) the app palette in LIGHT mode, where `--card` and `--background` are BOTH pure white and `--border` is a 92% grey, so `bg-card border` read as a featureless white block ("white on white", the owner's own guess, and the correct one), made to look like a floating SQUARE by (2) the height chain never resolving: the page root used `flex-1`, but the shell renders pages inside `<main className="min-h-0 flex-1">`, which is a plain BLOCK and not a flex container — so `flex-1` resolved against nothing, the board fell back to its `min-h-64` floor and the viewport below it stayed empty. `CanvasPage` fills that same slot with `h-full`, which is why the canvas never had the defect. **THE FIX.** (a) The page root is `flex h-full min-h-0 flex-col`, and every layer down to the editor now carries a definite height (`flex-1` body → `flex-1` section → `flex-1` surface → `height="100%"` editor, `shrink-0` on the header, the error banner and the Previous-drafts block); the editor's `minHeight` crutch is gone. (b) The writing surface takes the app's CARD edge — `rounded-lg bg-card ring-1 ring-foreground/10` — instead of `border`: the ring is 10% of the foreground, so it is a real line in light mode and a soft one in dark, which is exactly what a white surface on a white page needs. (c) `theme="none"` and `basicSetup={false}` are KEPT for parity with the canvas, and the honest reason is stated in code and in docs/21: they are not this bug's cause, but they leave ONE colour authority (`plainEditorTheme`) and remove CodeMirror's own highlight style. **THE EDITOR CONFIG BECOMES A TESTED SEAM.** The page-level test MOCKS CodeMirror, so an extension list that throws — or one that lost `history()` when `basicSetup` was turned off (which would make the page's Undo/Redo controls silent no-ops) — could reach the owner's browser with every test green. The set moved to `features/idea-board/editor.ideaBoardEditorExtensions` and is mounted for REAL (a raw `EditorView`, the `canvas-editor` precedent) in a NEW test file, which pins that it builds, that the `aria-label` reaches the content DOM, and that `undo` works through the exact command the Undo control dispatches; the page test additionally pins that the editor receives THAT seam by IDENTITY, so a private second list reds rather than drifting. **A DELIBERATELY REJECTED PIN, recorded so it is not re-added:** "no wiki chip in the board's rendered DOM" was rejected because CodeMirror builds decorations from the live VIEWPORT, which jsdom does not lay out — the absence could pass for the wrong reason; the plain-text property is pinned instead at the source (the seam imports neither `@codemirror/lang-markdown` nor any wiki decoration) with a non-vacuity half. **NUMBERS.** The landing gate (`bash scripts/gate.sh`, raw log `/tmp/gate-idea-board-4.log`, chunk logs `/tmp/gate-4129989`) printed **GATE GREEN, exit 0: 339 files / 3978 tests**, `chunk arithmetic: 339 of 339 test files covered`, lint 0 errors, typecheck clean, no `Errors:` line, peak RSS **1207 MB of the 3000 MB cap**; chunks `tests_lib 32/369 (882MB)`, `tests_llm 71/1158 (880MB)`, `tests_db 33/370 (659MB)`, `tests_domain 22/309 (649MB)`, `tests_features 137/1337 (1207MB)`, `tests_remainder 44/435 (1161MB)`. This slice adds **+1 file / +2 tests** over row 173's landing. **WHAT NO TEST HERE CAN PROVE, stated plainly:** jsdom computes no CSS and lays out no boxes, so the pins hold the PROPS and CLASSES that carry the fix (the seam identity, `h-full` on the root, the ring and `flex-1` on the surface) and the mechanism was verified by READING the installed package source; whether the surface now LOOKS right on the owner's screen is his eye's call, and the light-mode surface is intentionally identical in treatment to the module canvas. **COPIES: 1 — checked, no duplication (grepped `EditorView.theme`, `history()`, `wikiLinkDecorations` across `src/features/idea-board/`): the board's editor config is ONE named seam, and `plainEditorTheme` remains the one theme shared with the canvas (row 173).** | `src/features/idea-board/editor.ts` (NEW — the extension seam); `src/features/idea-board/IdeaBoardPage.tsx` (root `h-full`, the `shrink-0` chrome, the ring-edged surface, the seam import, `theme="none"`/`basicSetup={false}`); `tests/features/idea-board-editor.test.tsx` (NEW — the real mount + the source pin); `tests/features/idea-board.test.tsx` (the theme/height/seam/surface pin, the mock carrying props through); docs/21 (the two invariants + the corrected diagnosis), docs/18 §2.3 (the seam row amended with the invariants and the new NOT-Z entries); this row | The lesson is the DIAGNOSIS, not the CSS: I had a plausible, documented, precedent-backed cause ("the canvas comment says `theme=\"none\"` fixes the white slab") and the installable evidence contradicted it, so acting on it alone would have shipped a fix that changed nothing visible in the owner's light mode while looking like a faithful port of a proven fix. The corrected reading — app palette plus a collapsed flex chain — also explains why the canvas, which shares the palette, never had the symptom: it fills the slot. | active |

| 175 | **THE GATE'S ~12 MINUTES BECOME 7 M 53 S WITH NOTHING DROPPED — two chunks at once behind ONE combined-RSS watchdog, a diff-scoped fail-fast, and exactly two skips** (the problem was measured on the last full gate and NOT re-derived: `tests/features` was 442.59 s of a 706.6 s vitest phase and 44% of it framework overhead — transform 6.79 s, setup 17.92 s, import 97.76 s, tests 230.26 s, environment 78.84 s — and it was also the peak-RSS chunk at ~1.26 GB; every writer and the CoS serialized behind it on a box shared with the owner's other DSH project). **WHAT LANDED, all INSIDE `scripts/gate.sh`** — no second runner, no wrapper script, no CI copy, no test-selection mechanism outside it, because a second path is a new failure mode. **(1) Parallel chunks.** `tests/features` is split ROUND-ROBIN (not first-half/second-half: per-file cost varies and alphabetical order is arbitrary with respect to it) into `tests_features_a` (69 files) and `tests_features_b` (68), and at most TWO chunks run at once, each ONE worker in its OWN PROCESS GROUP via `setsid`. `setsid` is load-bearing, not decoration: bash background jobs otherwise inherit the script's process group, so a per-chunk kill would have killed the gate itself (measured: without `setsid`, the child pgid equals the shell pgid). `GATE_PARALLEL_CHUNKS=1` forces sequential. **(2) ONE watchdog over the combined groups.** Every second it sums `ps -o rss= -g` over all live chunks and kills ALL of them above `GATE_RSS_CAP_MB` (3000) or below `GATE_AVAIL_FLOOR_MB` (2500); a killed chunk is VOID, is re-queued and re-run SEQUENTIALLY, never counted, and `GATE_MAX_VOID_RETRIES` (default 1) makes a chunk that cannot fit the cap RED the gate instead of looping. A combined peak at 90% of the cap (`GATE_PARALLEL_FALLBACK_MB`, default 2700) makes the gate kill the pair and fall back to sequential BEFORE the kill line, and the summary states it. **(3) The arithmetic is still exact.** The union of all seven chunk file lists must equal the `tests/` walk with no path twice; a file no chunk picks up is a defect, not a saving. **(4) Fail-fast order + exactly two skips.** The diff is `origin/main` three-dot PLUS the working tree; changed files map to chunks (`src/lib`→`tests_lib`, `src/llm`→`tests_llm`, `src/db`→`tests_db`, `src/domain`→`tests_domain`, `src/features`→BOTH feature halves, other `src/*`→`tests_remainder`, a test file→its containing chunk) and the touched chunks run FIRST. A docs-only diff skips vitest ENTIRELY (lint + typecheck still run); a test-files-only diff runs ONLY the chunks that contain them; every other diff runs the full set. `GATE_PLAN_ONLY=1` prints the plan and runs nothing, so the mapping is reviewable without a 7-minute wait. **BEFORE → AFTER, same `9b925e3` tree.** vitest phase **706.6 s → 397 s** (-44%); whole gate **~12 min of chunks (≈783 s with today's 76 s of tooling) → 473 s / 7 m 53 s**; summed counts IDENTICAL at **339 files / 3978 tests**; lint 0 errors, typecheck clean, no `Errors:` line, nothing skipped. Per chunk (wall / peak, before → after): `tests_lib 53 s / 882 MB → 38 s / 837 MB`; `tests_llm 90 s / 880 MB → 96 s / 869 MB`; `tests_db 22 s / 659 MB → 25 s / 670 MB`; `tests_domain 18 s / 649 MB → 20 s / 726 MB`; `tests_features 442.59 s / 1207 MB → tests_features_a 225 s / 1216 MB + tests_features_b 245 s / 1188 MB` (concurrent, ~245 s of wall); `tests_remainder 81 s / 1161 MB → 84 s / 1108 MB`. The non-features chunks each cost a few seconds MORE under two-way contention (llm +6 s, db +3 s, remainder +3 s, domain +2 s) — that is the trade the overlap buys back several times over. **Combined peak RSS 1207 MB → 2295 MB of the 3000 MB cap** (765 MB headroom; the 2700 MB soft limit was never reached in the green run). **THE WATCHDOG IS PROVEN BY LOWERING ITS THRESHOLD, not by faking a spike.** (a) SOFT: `GATE_PARALLEL_FALLBACK_MB=400` on `tests/domain tests/db` → combined 776 MB → both chunks killed as VOID, summary `fell back to SEQUENTIAL after a 776MB combined peak`, both re-run green, `GATE GREEN`, `voided (re-run): 2`. (b) HARD: `GATE_RSS_CAP_MB=250 GATE_MAX_VOID_RETRIES=0` → combined 806 MB → both killed at peaks 396 / 410 MB, both VOID, not retried, `voided (re-run): 2`, `GATE RED`, and a `pgrep` afterwards showed NO orphan vitest. An honest 3000 MB spike was deliberately NOT staged: this slice is about load discipline and the brief forbids manufacturing load on a shared box. **THE `isolate: false` TRIAL IS A MEASURED NO.** vitest 4.1.11 DOES accept it as a CLI flag (`--no-isolate`), so NO config change was ever required or made. It was trialled on a NAMED SUBSET — the 14 `tests/features` files matching `board-*`, `canvas-*`, `chat-*`, the act()-heavy surfaces where the known cross-file console-hygiene flake family lives — under the SAME atomic lock, one worker, `--project jsdom`, heap-capped. Baseline isolated: **14 files / 148 tests, rc 0, 66 s**. Three sequential `--no-isolate` runs: **rc 1 EVERY time, the SAME 10 of 14 files failing, 57 / 72 / 64 failed tests, 43 s / 527 s / 52 s**. The failures are `vi.fn()` mocks not applied (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`) — mock/module-registry leakage across files sharing one worker, deterministic rather than load-timing. It saved only ~25-35% where it ran and costs 57-72 red tests, so it is REVERTED (by never adopting it); the isolated full gate is green at 339 / 3978. **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE.** No coverage guesswork: only the two skips above — no "run fewer chunks because the tests look unrelated", no sharding heuristics, no third runner, no CI copy, no `isolate` config change. **WHAT A MEASUREMENT CANNOT PROVE.** The BEFORE numbers are the last full gate's own figures on this tree, not re-derived (re-deriving them would mean a 12-minute run of a script that no longer exists); the AFTER numbers are this tree's own. The green run's 2295 MB combined peak does NOT prove a two-chunk pair can never approach 3000 MB on a differently loaded box — that is exactly what the soft fallback and the hard kill exist for, and neither was allowed to fire in the green run. The isolate canary is decisive for the flagged subset but is not an exhaustive statement about every jsdom file; the isolated FULL gate is the coverage evidence. And no test can prove the wall-clock win survives a box that is already loaded — only that it holds on this one at the measured moment. **COPIES: 1 — checked, no duplication (grepped `vitest run`, `campaigner-suite.lock`, `gate.sh`, `setsid` across the tree): the gate is still the ONE runner and the ONE lock, and the parallel/scoped logic lives inside `scripts/gate.sh`.** The `AGENTS.md` §Host hygiene 7 wording this needs is reported to the CoS rather than edited here (the CoS owns `AGENTS.md`). | `scripts/gate.sh` (the seven-chunk inventory, the round-robin split, the `setsid` launch, the combined watchdog with soft fallback and void re-queue, the exact arithmetic check, the diff-to-chunk selection and fail-fast ordering, `GATE_PLAN_ONLY`); docs/08 §The gate is a script + §Gate (new numbers and semantics); this row | The felt pain was serialization: every writer and the CoS queued behind ~12 minutes on a box shared with the owner's own DSH project, while 44% of the dominant chunk was framework overhead rather than assertions. Two chunks at ONE worker each keeps the total worker budget the config already allows (row 94) and overlaps the only long pole; the round-robin split is the deterministic load-balance choice. The watchdog stays honest by summing what is ACTUALLY live and treating any kill as VOID rather than evidence, and the fallback is the part that protects the shared box when the pair would crowd the cap. The isolate trial was kept because it could have been a real win (environment + import is exactly the 44%) and rejected on numbers: three red runs, the same ten files, mock leakage. Scope was limited to order plus two provable skips because a gate that guesses at coverage is worse than a slow one. | active |

The FIRST "before" measurement ran the five files as FIVE gate chunks (`/tmp/pilot-before/`), which pays a cold transform cache per process and OVERSTATES the saving (30.02 s → 16.14 s); the one-process A/B above is the honest comparator and is the number this row uses. **THE 3× CANARY.** The merged file then ran three more times sequentially under the gate: **32/32 green each**, lint 0 errors, typecheck clean, no `Errors:` line, durations **14.55 / 14.63 / 15.34 s** (`/tmp/pilot-canary-1..3/`) — stable, so the new adjacency introduced no flake. **THE HAZARD IS REAL AND IS WHY THE PILOT IS MOCK-FREE.** The `--no-isolate` trial (row 175) failed deterministically — the same 10 of 14 act-heavy files, `vi.fn()` mocks not applied — because files then share ONE module registry, which is exactly what a merge does inside one file. Two REAL cross-file leaks were nonetheless found and handled honestly rather than papered over: (1) `export-dialog`'s tests assign `URL.createObjectURL`/`HTMLAnchorElement.prototype.click` directly (not via `vi.spyOn`), which `vi.restoreAllMocks()` does NOT undo — the describe is placed in the MIDDLE of the merged file on purpose so the following `tree-scope`/`workspace` tests would have to survive the leak, and they did (3× canary); (2) the console-hygiene guard scopes its allowlist by `ctx.task.file.name` (`tests/setup.ts`), so ANY merged file whose originals rely on a file-scoped `ALLOWED_NOISE` entry would start failing under the merged file's name — none of the pilot's five relies on one, and this is a REQUIRED pre-check for every future cluster. **EXCLUDED FROM THIS PILOT, deliberately.** The act()-heavy family named in the brief — `board-*`, `canvas-*`, `chat-*`, `battle-*`, `creature-portrait-*`, `module-reader*`, `persona-run-ui*` — 20 files in `tests/features` (canvas 13, battle 2, module-reader 2, board 1, creature-portrait 1, persona-run-ui 1); it is the family the `--no-isolate` trial reddened and is deferred until the merge rule is proven on more no-mock clusters. **THE SWEEP RECOMMENDATION.** Merge, cluster by cluster, every group of ≥5 files that (a) shares ONE background (same helper/fixture imports and the same provider/Dexie mount), (b) has NO `vi.mock`, or an IDENTICAL mock target-set per file, (c) relies on no file-scoped `ALLOWED_NOISE` entry, (d) keeps the act()-heavy family out for now, and (e) keeps the merged file under **~120 tests** — past that a reviewer can no longer find a failure by name and the file stops being navigable, so a cluster that would cross 120 is SPLIT into two merges, not dropped. The value is resolved ONCE per run (the target's owning module, else the placement module) and threaded to the Cartographer brief, the per-room check, the stocking cap, the roster finalize/repopulate and the in-place fill. **THE THREE VALUES.** (1) `'system'` — compatibility: today's per-system behaviour (the numeric dnd5e band; verbatim for pathfinder2e). A module row WITHOUT the field reads here, so every legacy row is byte-identical. (2) `'pf2e-budget'` — PF2E-native numeric stocking: the fill grade is the share of Campaigner's OWN documented standard-encounter approximation (`pf2eStandardThreatLevels`, `2 × party level` creature-levels for a party of four, scaled by party size — deliberately NOT the dnd5e `T + 2` band), and a room that cannot reach its drawn share is a REPAIRABLE issue in the existing bounded repair turn, never silent. Retrieved GM Core excerpts are still obeyed VERBATIM in the prompt. (3) `'verbatim'` — ship no numbers; today's PF2E behaviour byte-identical, kept selectable because shipping no Paizo numbers is a deliberate licensing stance (docs/11 D12, docs/12 §13.2/§14). **THE DEFAULT IS SENSIBLE AND VISIBLE.** A `pathfinder2e` module defaults to `'pf2e-budget'`; every other system defaults to `'system'`. `createModuleAndRun` stamps it on the module row at creation (the New Module dialog shows the default and passes the explicit choice through the persisted `newModuleDraft` seam, campaign-tagged, kept by wipes, cleared on campaign delete), so every later generation/repopulate of that module reads the ROW — never live settings/dialog state — and a policy change months later cannot drift it. `encounterBudgetPolicy` on `moduleSchema` is additive optional (`.nullable().default(null)`, parse-on-read, no Dexie version). **THE LICENSING BOUNDARY.** No Paizo table is embedded anywhere; The request is therefore `{ castRank?, casterLevel? }`: the mob arc passes the pair for every spell with no branch, a cantrip ignores `castRank` (and says so in `warnings` when it was supplied), and a non-cantrip requires `castRank`. **THE PINNED RULE, per the source's own structure.** (1) `fixed`: the applied layer is the HIGHEST listed rank `<= appliedRank`; each layer's `damage` is a COMPLETE replacement (no base key survives), `area`/`target`/`duration` replace when the layer states them, and a layer key this rule does not consume is REPORTED in `warnings`; below the lowest layer the BASE applies. (2) `interval`: the improvement is a delta applied once per whole step, `appliedSteps = floor((appliedRank - rulesBaseRank) / interval)` — the exact expression the pinned reference implementation uses (`foundryvtt/pf2e` `v14-dev` `src/module/item/spell/document.ts`, `getDamage()`: `Math.floor((castRank - this.baseRank) / heightening.interval)`); `area` is a NUMBER of feet ADDED per step (`prepareBaseData`: `system.area.value += heightening.area * timesHeightened`). **WHERE THIS LANDING DELIBERATELY DIFFERS FROM THE BRIEF:** the brief asked for a LOUD ERROR when the cast rank is not a whole number of steps above the base. That rejects a LEGAL cast: a `(+2)` spell cast one rank higher gains NOTHING but is still castable, which is what floor means and what the pinned upstream does. So the rule applies the whole steps and REPORTS the arithmetic loudly — `appliedSteps` and `stepRemainder` are on the result and a leftover rank produces a named warning — instead of throwing. Corrupt arithmetic still throws: a non-positive/non-integer `interval`, a missing base damage entry for every stated delta, a formula it cannot read. (3) `cantrip`: the caller does not choose the rank; it auto-heightens to `clamp(ceil(casterLevel / 2), 1, 10)` (`document.ts` `rank`: `Math.ceil(this.actor.level / 2)` then `Math.clamp(…, 1, 10)`). Its RULES base rank is 1 — the corpus stores every cantrip at `system.level.value: 1` (MEASURED: Acid Splash, Ignition) — while `spellData.rank === 0` is row 181's deliberate LIST-ordering normalization; using 0 as the interval origin would over-heighten every cantrip by one step (Ignition at caster level 5 is `4d4`, not `5d4`), and that exact bug is pinned. (4) `prose-only`: a source with NO structured `heightening` but WITH parsed notes returns the applicable note text VERBATIM and the loud `PROSE_ONLY_MARKER`, with the BASE values and NO computed numbers — a missing structure is DISPLAYED, never guessed. A spell with neither structure nor prose is honestly flagged `base`. **NO INVENTED NUMBERS.** Formulas are combined SYMBOLICALLY, never evaluated and never rolled: same-die terms add their counts (`6d6 + 2x2d6` → `10d6`), different dice and flat bonuses stay separate, dice are ordered by FIRST APPEARANCE (base dice first, then any the delta introduces), the single flat total comes LAST (`1d6 + 1d4 + 4`), and an unreadable term (`@item.level`) throws. `heighteningUnparsed` is echoed in `unparsed` AND prefixed into `warnings`, never dropped. **THE PROVENANCE.** `source` is one of `base`/`fixed`/`interval`/`cantrip-auto`/`prose-only`; `valuesSource` names the arm that produced the numbers (`base`/`fixed`/`interval`) so a cantrip's auto rank and its numbers are BOTH reported; plus `appliedRank`, `appliedSteps`, `stepRemainder`, `notes` (verbatim applicable prose), `unparsed`, `warnings`, `structured`. **MEASURED UPSTREAM EVIDENCE (fetched, pinned as fixtures).** `packs/pf2e/spells/spells/cantrip/acid-splash.json` — `fixed` levels 3/5/7/9, each a COMPLETE replacement (`2d6`/`3d6`/`4d6`/`5d6`, splash `1`/`2`/`3`/`4`), base `1d6` + `1`; | 191 | **A FOCUS SPELL AUTO-HEIGHTENS — the importer stops claiming a rank it cannot know and the ONE heightening rule derives it in upstream's own order under its OWN `focus-auto` provenance** (measured by row 189's writer, recorded as a NAMED FOLLOW-UP in this ledger and docs/12 §5/§9 — the reason this row exists). **THE OWNER-VISIBLE DEFECT.** Upstream Foundry PF2e's `SpellPF2e.rank` getter (`foundryvtt/pf2e` @ `v14-dev`, `src/module/item/spell/document.ts`) is `const isAutoHeightened = this.isCantrip \|\| this.isFocusSpell; const fixedHeightenedRank = this.system.location.autoHeightenLevel \|\| this.spellcasting?.system?.autoHeightenLevel.value \|\| null; const heightenedRank = isAutoHeightened ? fixedHeightenedRank \|\| Math.ceil(this.actor.level / 2) \|\| null : this.system.location.heightenedLevel \|\| null; return Math.clamp(heightenedRank \|\| this.baseRank, 1, 10) as OneToTen;` — so a FOCUS spell is auto-heightened EXACTLY like a cantrip and `location.heightenedLevel` is IGNORED for it. Our side did not know: the bestiary adapter stamped a focus item's rank as `location.heightenedLevel ?? level.value`, `domain/mobSpells.mobSpellChips`'s auto arm was cantrip-only, and `domain/spellHeightening.spellAtRank` knew only `cantrip-auto`. **MEASURED EVIDENCE (row 189's, re-verified byte-for-byte at the real fixture):** Lawbringer Warpriest, level 5, "Athletic Rush" — `system.level.value: 1`, no `heightenedLevel` anywhere, both `spellcastingEntry` containers `autoHeightenLevel.value: null`, and upstream's rank for it is `clamp(ceil(5 / 2)) = 3`. Nothing in our corpus rendered that spell at 3. **THE TWO-LAYER FIX (row 183's split: the importer stamps the source's own data, the rule computes).** (1) THE RULE OWNS THE DERIVATION. `spellAtRank` gains a FOCUS arm, reached only when the spell carries the `focus` trait, is not a cantrip, and NO explicit `castRank` was requested. It derives upstream's order exactly — `request.autoHeightenLevel`, else `clamp(ceil(request.casterLevel / 2), 1, 10)` — and reports `source: 'focus-auto'` plus a new `focusAuto` boolean, mirroring `cantripAuto` and NEVER reusing `'cantrip-auto'`: the two are DIFFERENT rules and a chip's provenance line is the only place the owner can see which ran. AN EXPLICIT `castRank` WINS (the caller's assignment is authoritative): it takes row 183's ranked arm, `focusAuto` stays false, and neither the fixed rank nor the level is used. A focus spell's rules base rank is its OWN rank — only the cast rank is derived. A document carrying BOTH `cantrip` and `focus` rides the cantrip arm first, so row 183's behaviour is untouched. The bytes the model sees say: *when this creature's concept, name or intent implies a spellcaster — a wizard, priest, necromancer, druid, witch, shaman or any other spellcasting role — it MUST be given spells: cantrips plus the spells its level allows, chosen for the role from your own knowledge of what that role means (never narrow them by theme or school). A level-7 caster's DC would be derivable, and that is exactly the plausible-looking guess the marker refuses. **WHERE IT RENDERS.** The line is mounted on the ONE `features/campaign/components/stat-block.StatBlockCard` (the NPC card, the module reader, the artifact editor, the bestiary and the battle table all mount it), and through `lib/modulePdf.casterBoxSection` in BOTH PDF stat boxes (`statBoxContent` and `lib/pdfExport.statBlockSection`) — the SAME bytes on screen and on paper. A spell document carries `system.level` (**0 = cantrip — the system's own signal; there is no `cantrip` trait in 5e at all**), `system.school` (the system's eight codes `abj con div enc evo ill nec trs`, labels from its own `CONFIG.DND5E.spellSchools`), `system.properties` (vocal/somatic/material/concentration/ritual), activation/duration/range/target, the description HTML with its own `<strong>At Higher Levels.</strong>` (older docs: `<strong>Higher Levels.</strong>`) paragraph, and `activities.<id>.damage.parts[]` — each damage part with a `scaling` block (`mode: 'whole' / 'half' / ''`, `number`, `formula`). **IT IS THE SAME THIRD LANE, NOT A SECOND PARSER:** the adapter's `parseFileSync` now also emits `sections: PackSectionEntry[]` carrying the `spellData` payload, `packImport.sectionChunk` persists it as a `spell` chunk, and the adapter's own docstring documents the new fields — no new chunk type, no new lane, no new machinery. **THE 5e FILTER AXIS IS THE SCHOOL, AND IT IS THE SOURCE'S OWN.** The pre-arc page filtered PF2e *traditions*; The persona panel and the chain runner are **not** patched: every caller that sets `targetArtifactId` on a generate run reaches the seam, so a future caller cannot lose the level by rebuilding its input. `input` still WINS over the grounding, so the entity-batch paths apply the hint exactly once (no double-apply). **THE PARTY-LINE TRAP, CLOSED.** The fallback `level N` regex used to scan `input.brief`, and `buildEntityBrief` renders the app's generated party line (`partyLevelLine`: `Party of 4 adventurers at level N.`) into every encounter/npc brief — so an unrelated PARTY level could become the entity's level with no entity discrimination and no notice. The old sentence was wrong on its own terms: "a spell it cannot use" described a spell the app COULD use, whose values it computed correctly, penalised for a field our own request had demanded. **THE COMPATIBILITY PROMISE.** `mobSpellAssignmentSchema`/`statBlockSchema` stay the SUPERSET (`domain/mobSpells.mobSpellAssignmentSchema` re-exports `storedMobSpellAssignmentSchema()`), so every existing row parses unchanged: an already-saved NPC whose assignments carry the spurious field renders chips + a warning after this change with NO migration, and only the interpretation moved. | 207 | **THE THREE GENERATION READS THAT STILL CROSSED GAME SYSTEMS ARE SCOPED TO THE CAMPAIGN — the module PARTS rule excerpts, the module creator's bestiary window and the CAST that resolves it now read only the campaign's system's books, through ONE optional `system` on the creature pool; the UI/wiki-link callers stay deliberately unscoped, and a cross-system cast REFUSES loudly by name** (owner, verbatim: *"D&D imports should not be active when the current campaign is pathfinder and vice versa. THREE were not, and each is a real leak: (1) **module PARTS rule excerpts** — `llm/moduleGen.ruleExcerptSection` called `searchRules(query, { limit: 4, onEmbeddingProgress })` with NO `system` (`moduleGen.ts:2540` at `225142b`), and `searchRules` defaults to ALL ready books when the system is unset (`search/search.ts:64`), so a Pathfinder 2e campaign with a dnd5e pack installed grounded its module prose in dnd5e rules text; (2) **the module creator's bestiary window** — `llm/creatorRoster.collectCreatorRoster` → `db/creatureRepo.listLibraryCreatures()`, i.e. "every stat-block chunk of ANY book origin" (`moduleGen.ts:1030`; `creatorRoster.ts:127`), so the spine prompt offered the other system's creatures; (3) **CAST RESOLUTION, the dangerous one** — `features/modules/entity-batch.libraryCitationForEntity` (`:211`) read the SAME unscoped pool, so a pf2e module's bestiary slot naming a dnd5e-only creature resolved that dnd5e stat block INTO a pf2e npc. **THE FIX — ONE SEAM PER READ, AND READS (2) AND (3) SHARE ONE SEAM.** `db/creatureRepo.listLibraryCreatures(system?)` is the ONE creature pool: when `system` is given, a chunk is kept only when its OWNING BOOK's system matches (the chunk carries `bookId`; the books the pool names are read ONCE through `bulkGet` over the unique ids and indexed by id — never a read per creature). `collectCreatorRoster(targetLevel?, system?, …)` threads the campaign system through its existing injectable deps, `libraryCitationForEntity(entityName, slot, system?)` passes it to the same read, and `ruleExcerptSection(query, system, …)` passes `{ limit: 4, system }` to `searchRules`; `spineMessages` calls `collectCreatorRoster(mid, campaign.system)` and `partCall` passes `campaign.system`. Every `system` parameter is OPTIONAL, so a caller that omits it (and every pre-207 test) gets the every-book pool unchanged. **THE UI/WIKI-LINK DECISION (STATED, NOT SILENT).** The Rules page and the bestiary browser stay GLOBAL BY DESIGN — the owner may own several systems' books and browses them from one place — and the wiki-link publisher (`app/use-library-creatures`, `db/creatureRepo.wikiLinkCreatures`) stays unscoped, because an explicit `[[Zombie]]` reference is an explicit act and scoping it would turn a resolvable mention into a dangling link the moment the other system's book is also installed. All three therefore call the pool with NO system; only the generation reads above pass one, and that split is pinned. **A CROSS-SYSTEM CAST REFUSES LOUDLY AND BY NAME.** The existing no-such-creature throw IS the failure path: a system-scoped lookup that finds nothing says the library holds no creature of that name FOR THE CAMPAIGN'S SYSTEM while still naming the entity and the creature (`bestiary cast: the entity «X» asks to borrow the stats of «Y», but this workspace's library holds no creature of that name for Pathfinder 2e …`), lands in the batch's existing `failed[]` with its toast, and writes nothing — never a silent drop, never a substituted stat block. The scoped clause is APPENDED after the unscoped substring, so the two pre-existing `moduleGen-cast.test.ts` pins that assert `'no creature of that name'` (and every pre-207 exact-sentence pin) stay GREEN untouched (`tests/llm/moduleGen-cast.test.ts:647,1118`). A citation ALREADY recorded keeps resolving its own data unchanged (`domain/encounterResolve`/`db/monsterResolve` are untouched): the scope decides a NEW cast, it never rewrites history. A chunk whose book row is GONE cannot be attributed to the campaign's system and is therefore not offered (pinned) — the honest answer rather than a guess. **PINS (each names its own red).** (1) `tests/llm/moduleGen.test.ts` (the existing PARTS harness, real retrieval): two READY rules books, one per system, each carrying the part synopsis's own tokens plus a system-distinct marker sentence, so an unscoped search really returns BOTH (asserted as non-vacuity); a pf2e module's PARTS prompt carries only the pf2e marker, and the dnd5e mirror holds — removing `system` from `ruleExcerptSection` REDs it. (2) the SAME test's byte half: the pf2e prompt built against an own-system-only library is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the prompt built after the dnd5e book is installed — the no-behaviour-change requirement, proved rather than asserted. (3) `tests/llm/creatorRoster.test.ts` (the existing window harness): `collectCreatorRoster(3, 'pathfinder2e')` does not offer the dnd5e-only creature and the mirror holds, while the unscoped call still lists both — removing the scope REDs it. (4) `tests/features/entity-batch-creature-book.test.ts` (the existing cast harness): the pf2e cast of the dnd5e-only creature REJECTS with the entity, the creature AND the system named, the same-system cast resolves in both directions, and an unscoped caller keeps the pre-207 pool — replacing the throw with a silent drop REDs it. | 210 | **AN ALREADY-IMPORTED PACK IS VISIBLE IN SETTINGS — every fetch recipe row states its import state DERIVED LIVE FROM THE LIBRARY (the provenance URL first, the title fallback second, UNKNOWN rather than a guess), with row 204's per-lane breakdown, a `Re-import` action that stays ENABLED, and the system mismatch that hides a pack the same way** (owner's report, verbatim: *"When something is already imported (spells in my example) in settings, the fetch & import button should somehow indicate that fact. Right now its invisible which led to me confusion."*). **THE INTENT.** The card must answer "is this pack already in my library?" where the owner already looks, so a whole import's content (his spells) is never invisible until he infers it from an empty page — which is exactly the row-204 report one surface earlier. **THE MEASURED IDENTITY KEYS, re-derived at `e4c7840` before anything was touched.** A FETCHED book stamps provenance whose `sourceUrl` is `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<recipeId>` (`packFetch.ts:1003` — the fetched book is created and finalized by `importPack` through the same deps every manual import uses), so the recipe's `id` is the URL's TAIL inside the source's OWN repo — a proof, not a resemblance. A MANUAL file/zip import carries no provenance at all (`packMeta.sourceId` is set by `packImport` on every pack book, but `sourceUrl`/`fetchedAt` exist only on fetched ones), so the honest fallback is the book's `title` against the recipe's `label`, both through the app's ONE comparable form (`domain/artifactAlias.comparableName` — NFC, trim, case fold). **PROVENANCE FIRST, TITLE SECOND, AND WHY THAT ORDER:** a fetched curated pack's title IS its label (`packFetch` uses `curated.label`), so a book can match both keys; the provenance arm is checked first because it survives a rename (the owner may rename a fetched book) while the title arm is the only key a manual import can ever have. **THE STATES, and why no state is guessed.** (1) NOT IMPORTED → the row reads `Not imported yet.` and the button keeps `Fetch & import`; (2) IMPORTED → one proven match reads `Imported — fetched <ISO> · <row-204 lanes>` (a fetch stamp exists) or `Imported — updated <ISO> · <lanes>` (no fetch stamp — the row's own `updatedAt`, LABELLED `updated` rather than claiming a fetch time it does not have), and the button reads `Re-import`; (3) AMBIGUOUS → TWO OR MORE proven matches read `Import state unknown — N books in the library match this pack (…), so which one to report cannot be decided.` and state NO lane breakdown, never a pick; (4) UNIDENTIFIED → a book that only LOOKS like the recipe (its title reduces to the same letters+digits as the label — a manual import's derived slug `pathfinder-monster-core` against the label "Pathfinder Monster Core") carries neither provenance nor an exact title, so it reads `Import state unknown — 1 book in the library looks like this pack (…) but carries neither provenance nor a matching title, so none is proven to be this pack.` — NOT "not imported", because it might be (AGENTS rule 1); (5) LOADING → before the live read answers the row reads `Checking the library…`, never `Not imported yet.` **THE ACTION STAYS HONEST AND ENABLED.** Re-importing is a legitimate, documented remedy (docs/12 §15.4: a rules pack imported before the structured spell payload is indistinguishable from a stale one and needs a re-import — and fetching "again" creates a new book, docs/16 §5), so the control is never disabled and never re-scoped to a weaker verb; only a RUNNING fetch holds it, through the section's existing `BlockedControl` reason, unchanged. Use "Set system" on the Rules page to correct it.` — the imported state and its lanes stay visible beside it (the mismatch is additive, never a replacement). **CANDIDATES ARE THIS SOURCE'S READY PACK BOOKS.** Matching is restricted to `origin === 'pack' && status === 'ready' && packMeta.sourceId === source.adapterId`, which keeps the advanced "list everything" listing honest (two pf2e sources can offer the same repo folder), keeps a PDF book out of a pack question, and keeps an error book (packMeta stays null on a failed import) from ever reading as imported. **WHAT THIS ROW DID NOT CHANGE.** No import behaviour, no fetch recipe, no corpus read, no book classification, and NOTHING on the Rules page's own book list; | 209 | **A PACK PAYLOAD MUST AGREE WITH ITS ADAPTER'S DECLARED SYSTEM — the import boundary compares every emitted payload's own game system against `adapter.system`, refuses a disagreement LOUDLY through the existing failure report naming the entry and both systems, and every report states the system the pack went in as** (read-only probe at `225142b`, re-verified at `67a6e99`; the reserved board row 209, docs/20). **THE GAP, MEASURED.** A book's `system` is a CONSTANT per adapter — `packImport` writes `system: adapter.system` at `createBook` (docs/12 §6 step 2) — while the adapter's OWN payloads carry a game system: `StatBlock.system` (`domain/statblockFields.statBlockBaseFields`), `ItemData.system` (`domain/itemData`) and `SpellData.system` (`domain/spellData`). Every real adapter's literals agree today (`pf2e-foundry`/`pf2e-equipment`/`pf2e-conditions`/`pf2e-journal`/`pf2e-rules` → `pathfinder2e`; `dnd5e-foundry`/`dnd5e-equipment` → `dnd5e`) and NO adapter mixes systems or uses a display label — the payloads are schema-bound to `GameSystem` ids, so the check has no legitimate refusal to make (the STOP condition in the brief did not fire) — but NOTHING compared them, so a mis-chosen adapter (the manual pack dialog) could store a PF2e rules pack as dnd5e: INVISIBLE to every PF2e campaign (the spell corpus and row 207's scoped reads skip it) and fed to 5e ones. The mismatch is *visible* far away (system-named adapter labels, the Rules system badge) and *correctable* ("Set system", docs/12 §6) but was silent at the moment of import — the invisible-state class this row closes. **THE CHECK (ONE seam).** `packImport.claimedSystem` reads the system a payload CLAIMS; `packImport.systemAgreementFailure` produces the ONE refusal sentence; `packImport.partitionAgreeing` applies it to all three lanes (`entry.statBlock`, `entry.item`, `entry.spell`) in the parse loop, BEFORE any chunk is built. A disagreement becomes a `PackEntryFailure` in the SAME `failures` list the adapters' own per-entry problems use and is rendered by the EXISTING report — never a `console` line, never a silent drop, never a coerced payload. THE SENTENCE names the ENTRY (`file (name)`), the system it claimed and the adapter's declared system: `charau-ka.json (Charau-ka): the stat block is for game system "pathfinder2e", but adapter "…" declares "dnd5e"`; the report's existing lead-failure line and failed-entries list render it with no new surface. **ABSENT IS NOT DISAGREEMENT.** A rules-text `section` entry (a journal page, a condition, a feat) carries no structured payload and therefore makes NO system claim; `claimedSystem` returns `null` for it and the entry is accepted — the no-false-positive rule, pinned on a real conditions fixture. **STRICTNESS, reusing the importer's own failure path rather than inventing one.** SOME entries disagree → the agreeing REST imports and finalizes `ready`, with every refusal named in `failed[]` / `entriesFailed` (the importer's existing per-entry semantics). The WHOLE selection disagrees → zero valid entries, so the EXISTING zero-entry path fires: `failBook` + throw, leading with a representative refusal and the adapter's OWN `entryNoun` (`no valid creature or spell entries in the pack selection (0 skipped, 1 failed) — book … marked as error`). No second failure mechanism exists. **THE REPORT LINE.** `PackImportResult.system` is the adapter's DECLARED system; `features/rules/pack-lanes.formatPackSystem(system)` is the ONE spelling (`stored as Pathfinder 2e`, over `GAME_SYSTEM_LABELS`), rendered by the manual-import toast, the fetch toast and `PackImportReport` (a `pack-import-system` element). The line rides BESIDE row 204's ONE `formatPackLanes` breakdown, never inside it: the lane arithmetic, its wording and its call-site population are untouched, and no surface re-spells the system. **WHAT THIS ROW DELIBERATELY DID NOT CHANGE.** No adapter input, output or declared system; no parse schema; no `packMeta` field; no row-204 lane count or meaning; no corpus read; no row-207 scoping; no `formatPackLanes` call site; no `packFetch` behaviour (an agreement refusal simply makes an attempt yield fewer valid entries, and a real adapter never triggers one). The book's `system` is STILL the adapter's constant, and "Set system" is STILL the correction for a book already stored wrong (docs/12 §6). **WHAT A TEST CANNOT PROVE.** The check compares the systems payloads CLAIM; it does not detect a system from a document's own shape, so an adapter whose mapping stamped a wrong literal in BOTH its payload and its declaration would still agree — the pin proves the comparison, not the literal's correctness. No test proves the copy reads well to a person. **THE PINS AND WHAT EACH REDS ON** (`tests/ingest/packs/pack-import.test.ts`, the runner's EXISTING harness; the probes reuse the REAL adapters and the REAL fixtures, no second fixture set): (1) a REAL pf2e fixture (the `baseNpc` document) under a wrapper of the REAL `foundry-pf2e` parser declaring `dnd5e` hits the zero-entry path with `finalized` empty and the refusal sentence naming the entry and both systems; the mirror (the REAL dnd5e `ape.yml` fixture under a `pathfinder2e` declaration) asserts the dnd5e→pathfinder2e sentence and the adapter's own noun; (2) a correct import is unchanged and reports its system (`result.system === 'pathfinder2e'` for `foundry-pf2e`, `'dnd5e'` for `foundry-dnd5e-srd`, each equal to the `system` `createBook` was handed), and the rendered report line `stored as Pathfinder 2e` is asserted in `tests/rules-page.test.tsx` (report + toast) and `tests/features/bestiary-fetch-section.test.tsx`; (3) the no-false-positive pin: the REAL `foundry-pf2e-conditions` fixture (`blinded.json`, a `section` entry with NO spell payload) imports with zero failures and a `section` chunk; (4) a partial disagreement (a probe adapter emitting one `pathfinder2e` item beside one `dnd5e` item) imports exactly the agreeing one, names the refusal with its `file`/`name`/both systems, and finalizes `ready` with `entriesImported: 1` / `entriesFailed: 1`; (5) row 204's lane counts and their population pin are UNCHANGED (`tests/architecture/one-pack-lane-report.test.ts` still names exactly the formatter plus the four surfaces). **INJECTION-PROVEN, every arm's file hash printed with `git hash-object`, the suite lock held from BEFORE the first injection, the tree restored by a `trap` FROM HEAD (the slice is committed, so `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` is the correct restore):** A baseline `packImport.ts` `71c1ae6fcb6ce826bf898a6ca46abd6b9b5cc0ca` + `pack-lanes.ts` `566a95a89fa6c40fc0b51acd1f4bc0b63ef06411` → **GREEN 4 files / 46 tests**;
